chunks: And if you ask them, they will surely say, 'We were only engaging in idle talk and jesting.' Say, 'Was it with Allah and His signs and His messenger that you were mocking?'

key_terms.نَخُوضُ: engaging in idle talk or nonsense

ai.seo_question: What did the hypocrites claim when asked about their mockery of God and the Prophet?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited to demonstrate the superficiality of the hypocrites (Munafiqun) who used casual speech as a shield against accountability, a theme emphasized by Imam Ali in his sermons regarding the duality of their outward words and inward disbelief. The divine response, 'Is it Allah, His signs, and His Messenger that you were mocking?', serves as a definitive rebuttal to their claim of triviality, elevating their jest to a serious theological offense. This highlights the Shia scholarly view that mockery of the core tenets of faith, even if framed as humor, constitutes a rejection of divine authority.
